title: Action-cover Cech equalizers and natural recovery isomorphisms
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(P)$ and let $\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ be the category of internal actions: a sheaf $X$ with a natural unital associative action $C(S,J)\times X(S)\to X(S)$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Write $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, with the induced action when $T\in P_J$. Use the functors $\Phi$ and $G$ specified by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation, lem-sfb-profinite-action-free-restriction]. For each $T\in P_J$ the equivariant map $a_T:H(T)\to T$, $(j,t)\mapsto jt$, is a singleton cover. There is an equivariant homeomorphism
$$H(J\times T)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T)\times_TH(T),\quad (j,k,t)\longmapsto((j,kt),(jk,t)),$$
whose inverse sends $((j,u),(j',v))$ to $(j,j^{-1}j',v)$. Its two projections are $H(\alpha_T)$ and $H(\pi_T)\circ r_\gamma$, with $\gamma(k,t)=k$. For every sheaf $F$ on $P_J$, pullback $F(a_T)$ is a bijection from $F(T)$ onto
$$\{x\in G(F)(T):G(F)(\alpha_T)x=\gamma\cdot G(F)(\pi_T)x\}=Q_{G(F)}(T).$$
Under the equivariant Yoneda identification this yields a natural isomorphism $\eta_F:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi G(F)$. For every internal action $X$, the maps $e_{X,S}:\Phi(X)(H(S))\to X(S)$ given by evaluation at $(1,\operatorname{id}_S)$ are the components of an equivariant natural isomorphism $\epsilon_X:G\Phi(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}X$. Here naturality of $\eta$ includes all equivariant $u:T\to T'$, with $u a_T=a_{T'}H(u)$; the evaluation maps intertwine $\Phi(X)(r_g)$ with the given action of $g$ on $X(S)$. Both isomorphisms are natural in sheaf morphisms.

proof.text: The map $a_T(j,t)=jt$ is continuous by continuity of the given action. It is equivariant because $a_T(gj,t)=(gj)t=g(jt)$ for the free action on $H(T)$, and it is surjective since $a_T(1,t)=t$. Thus its singleton family is a covering by the stated finite jointly surjective covering rule. This uses no equivariant section of $a_T$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated action-cover infrastructure: verification of the covering used in the extracted presentation step 9

proof.text: Put $B=\{((j,u),(j^{\prime},v)):ju=j^{\prime}v\}$, the fiber product with its subspace topology and diagonal action. The map $c(j,k,t)=((j,kt),(jk,t))$ lies in $B$ because $j(kt)=(jk)t$. For a point of $B$, the equality $ju=j^{\prime}v$ gives $u=(j^{-1}j^{\prime})v$; hence $d((j,u),(j^{\prime},v))=(j,j^{-1}j^{\prime},v)$ satisfies $cd=1$ and $dc=1$. Both maps are continuous by continuity of multiplication, inversion and the action. Moreover $c(gj,k,t)=g\cdot c(j,k,t)$, so they give the required equivariant homeomorphism. The projections of $c$ are $(j,k,t)\mapsto(j,kt)=H(\alpha_T)(j,k,t)$ and $(j,k,t)\mapsto(jk,t)=(H(\pi_T)\circ r_\gamma)(j,k,t)$, with exactly the right-translation convention in the cited statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated infrastructure: explicit two-sided inverse and projections for the action-cover fiber square

proof.text: Apply the defining sheaf equalizer to the singleton cover $a_T$. It identifies $F(T)$, by $F(a_T)$, with the equalizer of the two pullbacks $F(H(T))\rightrightarrows F(B)$. Since $F(c)$ has inverse $F(d)$ by functoriality and $cd=dc=1$, applying $F(c)$ preserves and reflects equality. The two arrows therefore become $F(H(\alpha_T))$ and $F(r_\gamma)F(H(\pi_T))$; contravariance fixes this order. By the cited free-restriction statement these are $G(F)(\alpha_T)$ and $\gamma\cdot G(F)(\pi_T)$. Thus the equalizer is precisely $Q_{G(F)}(T)$, as an equality of sections on the entire profinite parameter $J\times T$.

source.place: Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets, equation-sheaf-condition; specialize to the singleton action cover and use step 2

proof.text: Let $q_{X,T}:\Phi(X)(T)\to Q_X(T)$ be the evaluation bijection in the cited Yoneda statement. Define $\eta_{F,T}=q_{G(F),T}^{-1}\circ F(a_T)$, with $F(a_T)$ corestricted to the equalizer of step 3. Both factors are bijective. For an equivariant $u:T\to T^{\prime}$, one has $u a_T=a_{T^{\prime}}H(u)$, since $u(jt)=ju(t)$. Consequently $F(H(u))F(a_{T^{\prime}})=F(a_T)F(u)$. The cited statement identifies restriction on $Q$ with $G(F)(u)=F(H(u))$, so this equality is the naturality square for $\eta$. Its componentwise inverse is natural by composing this square with the two inverses. Hence $\eta_F$ is a sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated recovery: construction and object-naturality of the first recovery isomorphism

proof.text: For a sheaf morphism $v:F\to F^{\prime}$, naturality at $a_T$ gives $v_{H(T)}F(a_T)=F^{\prime}(a_T)v_T$. Free restriction makes $G(v)_T=v_{H(T)}$, and the Yoneda identification makes the induced map on $Q$ this same component. Applying $q^{-1}$ therefore gives $(\Phi G(v))_T\eta_{F,T}=\eta_{F^{\prime},T}v_T$. This proves naturality of the first recovery isomorphism in the sheaf variable.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated recovery: naturality of the first recovery isomorphism in sheaf maps

proof.text: Take $\epsilon_{X,S}=e_{X,S}$ from the cited free-evaluation bijection. Its explicit inverse sends $x\in X(S)$ to $b_x$ with $(b_x)_V(a,b)=a\cdot b^*x$. For a continuous $f:V\to S$, restriction along $H(f)$ followed by evaluation gives $b_V(1,f)=X(f)(b_S(1,\operatorname{id}_S))$, by naturality of the sheaf map $b$. For an equivariant sheaf map $w:X\to Y$, postcomposition gives $(w\circ b)_S(1,\operatorname{id}_S)=w_S(e_{X,S}(b))$. These identities prove naturality in both the profinite parameter and the internal-action variable; the explicit inverse gives the inverse underlying sheaf map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated recovery: free-evaluation bijection and its two naturality squares

proof.text: It remains to verify the action on this sheaf isomorphism. By free restriction, $g:S\to J$ acts on $G\Phi(X)(S)$ by $\Phi(X)(r_g)$. This sends $b:h_{H(S)}\to X$ to $b\circ h_{r_g}$. Its evaluation is $b_S(g,\operatorname{id}_S)=g\cdot b_S(1,\operatorname{id}_S)$: equivariance of $b$ applied to $g\cdot(1,\operatorname{id}_S)=(g,\operatorname{id}_S)$ gives the equality. Thus $e_{X,S}(\Phi(X)(r_g)b)=g\cdot e_{X,S}(b)$ for every profinite $S$ and every continuous $g$, rather than just constant $g$. Bijectivity makes the inverse equivariant as well: apply this equality to $b=e_{X,S}^{-1}(x)$. Together with steps 6 and 5 this gives both asserted natural recovery isomorphisms.
